facts.text: Gutterballs was made for about $250,000 — and shot in just three weeks in the summer of 2007.
The film premiered January 18, 2008 at Fangoria's Weekend of Horrors, three months before its DVD release.
Director Ryan Nicholson called the movie "a love letter to the kind of horror movies I grew up watching."
Nicholson was a working makeup FX artist on Final Destination, Scary Movie and Blade Trinity before directing. Gutterballs was his follow-up to 2006's Live Feed.
The disco-themed Xcalibur Bowling Centre is a real multi-million-dollar bowling center, which gave this tiny production a lot of free production value.
Nicholson pitched the film's tone as a gory adult version of Scooby-Doo.
The word "fuck" is said 516 times, the most of any scripted film. Overall only a few documentary and Wolf of Wall Street-type titles beat it.
Much of the dialogue was improvised, which may explain the cussing count.
Most of the gore was shot in a separate studio so fake blood wouldn't wreck the real bowling alley.
The killer's phone number, 976-3845, spells 976-EVIL, a nod to the 1988 slasher 976-EVIL.
The MPAA told Nicholson nearly 20 minutes had to go to dodge an NC-17. He released the film unrated instead.
The poster and promo campaign are a deliberate homage to the 1980 cult slasher Maniac.
The film is set in the 1980s, but eagle-eyed viewers spot a Daytona USA arcade cabinet (1993-94) and modern Pepsi logos.
Most of the movie was shot in sequence, but the two rival bowling teams mostly filmed on separate days.
The Italo-disco score credits "Gianni Rossi", which is actually a pseudonym for Steve Moore.
The 2009 TLA Releasing DVD came with an altered soundtrack compared to the 2008 Plotdigger original.
Nicholson has said the violence is meant to be cartoony, campy overkill, like getting strangled to death by bowling shoes.
Nicholson cites slashers, giallo and exploitation horror from his childhood, plus Joe Dante and David Cronenberg, as influences.
The smoke from the waxing machine was added digitally in post-production.
Goof hunters note that in many close-ups of the dead bodies you can see the actors breathing.
A cut-down German release lost about 15 minutes for SPIO/JK approval. The FSK 'not under 18' retail version lost roughly 26.
Wade Gibb, who plays Joey, was born in High Level, Alberta, and grew up on a grain farm.
A 2011 'Pin-Etration Edition' with hardcore inserts was limited to just 69 copies.
Reviewers compared it to Troma: DVD Talk called it 'a damn fine sexually explicit, graphically violent, morally repugnant, willfully bad B movie.'
Mihola Terzic, who plays Sarah, is also a professional model and a published poet.
The film got a sequel, Gutterballs 2: Balls Deep, which premiered at Texas Frightmare Weekend in May 2015.
The soundtrack includes tracks by Patrick Coble, such as 'Wax-O-Matic' and 'Hot Body Storage'.
The credits were reportedly shot in Surrey, British Columbia, a suburb of Vancouver.
During the end credits, BBK's identity is shown after every murder scene.
